name: unknown-event-dropped
description: an event type the client does not recognise is dropped with a warning and the run survives
kill: return `of(event)` instead of `EMPTY` from the `!isRecognizedEvent` branch in enforceEvents — the warning is still emitted and the run still completes, so `outcome`, `warnings`, `messageCount` and `messages` all stay green and only `eventTypesAbsent`/`eventTypes` catch it: FUTURE_EVENT reaches application code. Failing the run on an unrecognised type instead kills the `completed` expectation.

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client's event surface is ChatResponseUpdate.RawRepresentation, and the builder-only events yield no update: TEXT_MESSAGE_START and TEXT_MESSAGE_END open and close the message being assembled and hand a consumer nothing, so they cannot appear in a delivered list however faithfully the client processes them. The list here is the base list minus exactly those; every event this fixture is actually about is still in it, in order. The rule itself is untouched: `eventTypesAbsent` is inherited from the base, so FUTURE_EVENT still must not reach application code on this lane.
